messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Fit a new bathroom suite replacing the old one", "project": "House in England", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "Sch 4 para 1(j)", "document": "BR2010", "text": "Work consisting of— (j) replacing— (i) a sanitary convenience with one that uses no more water than the one it replaces, (ii) a washbasin, sink or bidet, (iii) a fixed bath, (iv) a shower, (v) a rainwater gutter, or (vi) a rainwater downpipe,where the work does not include any work to underground drainage, and includes no work to the hot or cold water system or above ground drainage, which may prejudice the health or safety of any person on completion of the work;"}, {"ref": "para 11.2", "document": "ADL1-2021", "text": "11.2 Renovation of a thermal element means one of the following. a. Providing a new layer through cladding or rendering the external surface of a thermal element. b. Providing a new layer through dry-lining the internal surface of a thermal element. c. Replacing an existing layer through stripping down the element to expose basic structural components (e.g. bricks, blocks, rafters, joists, frame) and then rebuilding. d. Replacing the waterproof membrane on a flat roof. e. Providing cavity wall insulation."}, {"ref": "para 3.29", "document": "ADF1-2021", "text": "3.29 For a new wet room, ventilation location should follow paragraphs 1.9 to 1.31, performance testing should follow paragraph 1.32 and controls should follow paragraphs 1.33 to 1.37. Building Regulations 2010 F1(1) Refurbishing a kitchen or bathroom in an existing dwelling NOTE: If a combustion appliance is installed in a kitchen or bathroom where building work is carried out, Part J of the Building Regulations must be considered."}]}

message.content:
Replacing a bathroom suite like-for-like is **not notifiable**. It falls within the non-notifiable work in Schedule 4 para 1(j) of the Building Regulations 2010. That paragraph covers replacing:

- a WC with one that uses no more water,
- a washbasin,
- a fixed bath,
- a shower.

The condition is that the work does not touch underground drainage. It also must not involve work to the hot or cold water system or above-ground drainage that could prejudice health or safety.

Nothing in the description suggests a new wet room, new drainage runs or a combustion appliance. Refurbishing an existing bathroom does not trigger the new wet room ventilation provisions in
message.reasoning: Replacing a bathroom suite like-for-like falls under Schedule 4 para 1(j), so it's generally not notifiable, though it could change if the new WC uses more water or drainage layout changes are involved.
